title: Edge Computing
subtitle: Processing data on the device vs sending to the cloud

content.text: Sending all raw sensor data to the cloud is expensive and slow. Edge computing processes data locally on the device, sending only summaries or alerts.

content.code:
import statistics
from collections import deque

# Keep a rolling window of 60 readings (5 mins @ 5s interval)
window = deque(maxlen=60)

def process_reading(raw_temp: float):
    window.append(raw_temp)

    # Only send data to cloud if anomaly detected
    if len(window) >= 10:
        avg = statistics.mean(window)
        stdev = statistics.stdev(window)

        if abs(raw_temp - avg) > 2 * stdev:
            # Anomaly: send immediately
            cloud_send({"alert": "anomaly", "value": raw_temp, "avg": avg})
        elif len(window) == 60:
            # Normal: send 5-minute summary once per window
            cloud_send({"avg": avg, "min": min(window), "max": max(window)})

content.text: Classify data at the edge: only send anomalies in real time; batch aggregate normal data to reduce cloud costs by 10-100x.

questions.question: What is the main benefit of edge processing?
options: Reduced data volume to the cloud, lower latency for decisions
Longer battery life of the broker
questions.explanation: Processing data locally reduces the volume sent to the cloud, cutting bandwidth costs and enabling faster local decisions.
